proposals.before: Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, a member of the imperial clan, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunli and was registered in the Bordered Blue Banner.
proposals.after: Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, a member of the imperial clan, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunti and was registered in the Bordered Blue Banner.
proposals.reason: 允禵 is Yunti; Yunli misreads 禵.

proposals.after: Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, an imperial clansman, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunti and belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner.

proposals.before: For his service he was made Second-rank Defender Prince of the State and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

proposals.after: Under the Tongzhi emperor he was raised to First-rank Defender General of the State and made an Inner Minister.

proposals.after: and his grandson Yuzhao held the rank of First-rank Supporter General of the State.

proposals.before: Yishan later surrendered the northeastern frontier as well, and the damage he left was even worse.
proposals.after: Yishan later again abandoned the northeastern frontier lands, and the harm he left was even deeper.
proposals.reason: 棄 means abandon, not surrender; 復 means again; 尤深 is especially deep. The idiomatic rendering softens and slightly shifts the sense.

decisions.reason: s0001 names the ancestor 允禵. The character 禵 is tí (Yunti); Yunli would require 禮 (as in 允禮). The proposed Yunti corrects a real romanization error without changing the rest of the accurate idiomatic wording.
The same s0001 phrase 允禵 must be Yunti in the literal as in the idiomatic. Yunli misreads 禵; the proposed replacement is the correct reading and otherwise preserves the literal sentence.
s0036 awards 二等鎮國將軍. 鎮國將軍 is a Qing imperial-clan general rank, not a princely title; replacing "Prince" with "General" restores the correct office while keeping the rest of the sentence.
s0058 has 封一等鎮國將軍. As in r0003, 鎮國將軍 is a general rank of the imperial clan, not a prince; "First-rank Defender General of the State" matches the Chinese.
s0063 states 孫毓照，一等奉國將軍. 奉國將軍 is likewise an imperial-clan general rank, not a prince; the proposed "Supporter General" corrects that error without rewriting the surrounding kinship phrasing.

s0174 reads 奕山後復棄東北邊地，其貽患尤深. 棄 is abandon (not surrender), 復 is again, and 東北邊地 / 貽患尤深 support "northeastern frontier lands" and deeper/especial harm. The prior "surrendered…as well…even worse" misstates the verbs and softens 復; the proposed wording restores those senses in natural English.
